destination.title: Inflationary information problems and entropy prescriptions
destination.question: When do inflationary entropy accounts indicate an information problem, and how do thermal assumptions or state-counting prescriptions change that assessment?
destination.summary: Thermal horizon radiation and stochastic inflaton information require separate entropy accounts. Volume weighting is a proposed prescription; exact de Sitter equilibrium does not automatically produce a radiation entropy paradox.

systems: Horizon radiation seen by a static observer
targets: An information formulation of an e-folding bound
Proposed entropy behavior under volume weighting
regimes: Exact de Sitter thermal equilibrium
Slow-roll backgrounds with changing light-state content
Stochastic eternal inflation
assumptions: The stochastic Shannon-entropy identification requires the stated classicalization and coarse-graining setup
Volume weighting is justified by a proposed global typicality prescription
The radiation-only analysis separately assumes black-hole production is forbidden
conventions: Thermal entropy, stochastic Shannon entropy and geometric entropy have distinct roles
Information paradox and complementarity are separate diagnostics
includes: Conditional absence of a radiation information paradox
excludes: A universal resolution of the de Sitter information problem
Automatic information loss from horizon radiation

sources.title: Stochastic inflation and entropy bound in de Sitter spacetime

evidence.text: Relate the field distribution to the momentum marginal of a Wigner function; compare Gaussian entropies through a symplectic eigenvalue ν. For volume weighting, use an approximate WKB solution at small noise strength α. An appendix derives a Lindblad equation first for a quadratic potential.

sources.title: Stochastic inflation and entropy bound in de Sitter spacetime

evidence.text: Weight stochastic histories by exp[3∫Hdt] and normalize the result. The volume-weighted equation adds 3(H−⟨H⟩_V)P_V to the local Fokker–Planck evolution. The authors identify this history-dependent expansion effect as non-Markovian.

sources.title: Stochastic inflation and entropy bound in de Sitter spacetime

evidence.text: Use the stochastic Langevin equation dφ/dt=−V′/(3H)+H^{3/2}η/(2π), with normalized delta-correlated white noise, and its Fokker–Planck description for the local distribution P(φ,t).
